ideas.pitch: A predictive dashboard utilizing Poisson regression and rolling backtests to forecast bus crowding and emissions across Rutgers campus routes based on weather, class schedules, and event data.
ideas.title: Rutgers Campus Transit Demand & Carbon Forecaster
ideas.why_it_could_win: Matches the proven predictive modeling and safety forecasting pattern of past winning projects like ai-incident-forecasting, appealing strongly to university-level evaluators looking for practical campus utility.

ideas.pitch: An automated platform combining graph intelligence and LightGBM to monitor campus smart devices and IoT networks, highlighting potential security vulnerabilities and compliance risks.
ideas.title: ScarletSecure: Rutgers IoT Device Anomaly & Risk Detector
ideas.why_it_could_win: Leverages the winning formula of combining graph intelligence and explainable machine learning seen in top financial and industrial monitoring hackathon winners.

ideas.pitch: A localized nutrition tracking app that scans Rutgers dining hall menus, optimizes daily meal choices based on student fitness goals, and tracks food waste metrics for sustainability.
ideas.title: DiningHall AI: Rutgers Sustainable Nutrition Assistant
ideas.why_it_could_win: Replicates the practical, consumer-facing health utility that secured first prize at the Mealzy 24-Hour Hackathon, targeting an immediate student pain point.

ideas.pitch: An autonomous agent platform that automates club budgeting and reimbursement payouts using USDC escrow smart contracts on Base, removing administrative friction for student organizations.
ideas.title: KnightPay: Autonomous Student Club Expense Escrow
ideas.why_it_could_win: Directly applies the autonomous agent and escrow pattern that won the Synthesis Hackathon Locus track, offering tangible administrative utility for university groups.

ideas.pitch: A multi-agent student support system utilizing LangGraph and RAG to match Rutgers course codes with personalized AI tutor agents and verified student study materials.
ideas.title: StudyMesh: Multi-Agent Peer Tutoring & Resource Hub
ideas.why_it_could_win: Mirrors the architecture of the GreenNovation Hackathon winner by deploying specialized multi-agent workflows to solve educational coordination problems.
